samples.text:
The maps show the area around a railway station in 1995 and after it was redeveloped in 2025. Overall, the area became more modern, with many new building and better transport facilities, but the station and the railway did not change.

In 1995 there was the station next to the railway and a small road went from it to Station Road in the north. In the west there was a goods depot and in the east a car park. On the other side of Station Road there was a post office. In the south, below the railway, all the land was disused.

In 2025, the road from the station has been replaced by a station square. The car park has changed into a bus interchange and a taxi rank. Also, the goods depot become an office block and the post office became a hotel. The disused land was used for apartments in the south-west, a park in the middle and a new car park in the south-east. Finally, there is a footbridge which cross the railway from the park to station.
samples.why: Overview present but general · all main changes covered in a list-like way · formulaic linking · adequate vocabulary · several errors in plurals, tense, agreement and articles, none impeding meaning.

samples.text:
The maps compare the area surrounding a railway station in 1995 with the same area after its redevelopment in 2025. Overall, the site has been transformed from a partly industrial and underused area into a modern transport hub with housing, offices and green space, although the railway, the station and Station Road have been retained.

North of the railway, the short road linking the station to Station Road has been replaced by a pedestrian station square. The car park to the east of the station has been converted into a bus interchange and a taxi rank, while the goods depot to the west has made way for an office block. On the opposite side of Station Road, the post office has been replaced with a hotel.

The biggest change, however, can be seen south of the railway, where a large area of disused land has been completely developed. Apartments now occupy the western part of this land, with a park in the middle and a car park to the east. In addition, a footbridge has been constructed over the railway, connecting the park with the station.
samples.why: Clear overview · key features logically grouped north and south of the railway · varied linking · good vocabulary (transport hub, made way) · mostly error-free sentences.

samples.text:
The maps depict the area around a railway station before and after its redevelopment, in 1995 and 2025 respectively. In essence, a district of industrial and disused land has been regenerated into a mixed-use area centred on public transport, with the railway line, the station and Station Road the only features left intact.

To the north of the railway, the changes have largely involved converting existing sites. The access road that ran from the station up to Station Road has been replaced by a pedestrianised square, and the car park immediately east of the station has been divided between a bus interchange and a taxi rank. Similarly, the goods depot on the western side has given way to an office block, and across Station Road the post office has been replaced by a hotel.

South of the tracks, a formerly disused stretch of land has been developed for the first time. Its western portion is now occupied by apartments, the centre by a park and the eastern end by a car park. These new facilities are linked to the station by a footbridge spanning the railway line from the park.
samples.why: Clear, perceptive overview · changes skilfully grouped by conversion versus new development · cohesion handled naturally · precise vocabulary (regenerated, mixed-use, spanning) · wide range of accurate structures.
